permissionCapabilities.evidence: Installed native CLI --help and app-server generate-json-schema, both executed with sandbox-exec blocking user filesystem writes. Schema files were generated in and removed from a dedicated temporary directory. No thread, turn, model prompt, permission changes, or runtime sandbox test was performed.

nonSelectableApprovalValues.untrusted: Schema can represent it, but current official configuration documentation says it cannot be selected directly; stricter behavior may be derived from an untrusted project.
nonSelectableApprovalValues.on-failure: Not exposed by the installed CLI or generated AskForApproval enum; official configuration documentation marks it deprecated.

granularApproval.semantics: true allows approval prompts in that category to surface; false auto-rejects that category. It does not automatically approve the action.

semantics: Sandboxing controls execution boundaries; approvalPolicy controls whether crossing those boundaries can ask for review. Do not equate never with disabling the sandbox.

read-only is the native filesystem restriction mode; workspace-write permits workspace modifications and routine local commands within the boundary; danger-full-access removes native filesystem and network sandbox boundaries.
on-request permits requests to cross a sandbox boundary; never does not pause for approvals, so denied sandbox operations fail rather than silently obtaining broader access.
auto_review changes who reviews eligible approval requests and does not by itself expand writable roots, enable network access, or review actions already allowed inside the sandbox.
Current configured policies remain subject to executor and organization requirements. A UI selection alone is not proof that a requested runtime policy was applied.
Host process-level isolation and native executor sandboxing are separate controls; local worktree separation alone is not an OS sandbox.
